approval_source.question_set: Where each host's alert URL and escalation URL point

reason: The monitoring services approval left both URLs unset. The monitor job POSTs the same JSON to the alert URL when an alert fires and when it resolves, so a heartbeat-service ping URL, which marks its check up on every request, cannot carry alerts. The escalation URL receives only a severity 1 alert still firing after 15 minutes, once, so a heartbeat check's failure URL can carry it.

decisions.question: P01_E05_MONITORING_SERVICES_2026-10-12, unset: the alert URL
decisions.selected: An ntfy.sh topic with a secret name
decisions.rule: Each host's alert_url is an https ntfy.sh topic URL whose topic name is a random 256-bit value. Every firing and resolved alert arrives on the founder's phone as a push notification carrying the alert JSON. The topic name is the only secret: it lives only in each host's owner-only monitor settings file and the founder's own records, never in the repository or in chat. Free, no account, and no change to the monitor job. A leaked name is replaced by a new topic and a new settings file (monitor-settings.sh).

decisions.question: P01_E05_MONITORING_SERVICES_2026-10-12, unset: the escalation URL
decisions.selected: A Healthchecks.io check's failure URL, alerting the backup person by e-mail
decisions.rule: Each host's escalation_url is the /fail URL of one Healthchecks.io check named escalation, whose integration e-mails the backup person. The monitor job sends a severity 1 alert still firing after 15 minutes there, once; the check goes down and the backup person is e-mailed. There is no acknowledgement: an alert that keeps firing for 15 minutes escalates. Free and no change to the monitor job; the backup person installs nothing. The founder resets the check after the incident.

unset: The backup person, a root key holder named outside this repository
The status page monitor, once the sentry has its final address
does_not_authorize: any run on a real host
